subject.title: Feature Request: Cross-platform migration tool (migrate export/import)

question: Should OpenClaw core own automated same-product archive export/import for moving an existing install, or keep core to backup/export/verify/convert plus user-driven restore?
rationale: The choice controls CLI namespace, archive trust, secret/session portability, destructive write policy, and whether the linked implementation should be reviewed, narrowed, or closed.

options.title: Scope a minimal native import contract
options.body: Define a preview-first core export/import lifecycle with canonical target validation, secret/session policy, rollback/conflict handling, and security-focused tests before implementation.

options.title: Prefer backup conversion and manual restore
options.body: Improve backup platform targeting, archive conversion, verification, and docs while keeping destructive restore steps user-driven for now.

options.title: Route optional pieces outside core
options.body: Keep core to missing APIs and let plugins, skills, or ClawHub packages own optional cloud, scheduled, encrypted, or workspace-specific migration flows.

recommendation.title: Scope a minimal native import contract
recommendation.body: Define a preview-first core export/import lifecycle with canonical target validation, secret/session policy, rollback/conflict handling, and security-focused tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: They are tied to backup safety hardening and already raised the core restore/import security-boundary concern in the prior implementation discussion.
